transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Uh... yeah. Just... having some trouble, I guess. 

I just... I can’t stop jumping out of my skin lately. Like at work, if a breaker snaps loud, or... a tool drops. Or if somebody just comes up behind me. I just jump. And my heart keeps hammering... long after everyone else has already moved on. 

So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Are you feeling anxious all the time, or is it mainly in response to specific events or noises like the ones you mentioned?

I don't know... it's kind of all the time, I guess. Not just the noises. 

I just... I walk around mad, mostly. And... guilty. Just feels like I failed that kid... and everybody can just see it on me. So... yeah.
Is the feeling of guilt you mentioned related to something specific that happened, or is it more of a general feeling?

Yeah... it’s, uh... it's tied to something specific. Just... something that happened. 

I don't really... I don't want to get into the details of it right now. Just... a bad situation. That's all.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Uh... about a year and a month now. Give or take. 

Ever since... well, since the arc-flash accident. On that retrofit job. Just... been going on since then.
Do you find that you get anxious or jump out of your skin when you're reminded of the arc-flash accident?

Yeah... I guess so. That's kind of why I'm here. 

Just... if a breaker snaps loud, or somebody drops a wrench on the concrete... even if a guy just walks up behind me when I'm working... I just jump. Can't help it. And then my chest just... my heart just keeps hammering for a long time after. Even when everybody else just goes back to work. So... yeah.
Do you ever find yourself reliving the arc-flash accident, like it's happening all over again?

Yeah. Um... sometimes. 

It just... it happens out of nowhere. I could just be... I don't know, just loading tools in the back of the truck. And suddenly I just... I see that flash in my head. Or I hear the trainee yelling. 

It just... it knocks me sideways. Like... like it's happening right then. I try not to think about it, but... yeah.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of the arc-flash accident?

Yeah... I guess. I just... I make excuses, mostly. Like, not to go near certain panels, or... breakers. Some job sites, too. I just find a way not to be around them. 

And... I don't really like talking about that day, either. It's just... once it starts up in my head, I can't shut it off. So I just try to stay away from all of it.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself when you're reliving the arc-flash accident?

No... I don't think so. 

I'm not watching it from somewhere else. I'm just... I'm right back in it. So... no.
Do you ever feel numb or disconnected from the world around you when you're not reliving the arc-flash accident?

No... I don't really get that. 

I mean... I'm just trying to get through the day, mostly. I don't think I feel... numb. Just... I don't know. No.
Are there any everyday activities or things you used to enjoy that you've stopped doing because of what happened?

Yeah... mostly everything. 

I used to... I'd be the guy staying late to fix up cars, or... play ball. Help the young techs learn the ropes. But... I don't do any of that now. I just... I sit at home. People call, and I just let the phone ring. It just... none of it feels worth starting.
Do you avoid thinking or talking about your feelings related to the arc-flash accident?

Yeah. I mean... I don't talk about it. 

I just... I make excuses if people bring it up. Or if I have to go near certain panels or... breakers at work. Job sites. I just try to stay away from it all. Because... if I start thinking about it, or talking about it... it just starts playing in my head. And I can't... I can't shut it off once it starts. So I just... avoid it.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to care about since the arc-flash accident?

Yeah, I guess. Like I said before... I just don't do much anymore. Used to mess around with cars, play some ball... help the new guys out at work. Now I just sit around the house. Don't even pick up the phone. Just... don't see the point in any of it now.
Do you often find yourself thinking that you could have done something to prevent the arc-flash accident?

Yeah... I guess. 

I don't know, I just... I walk around mad all the time. And... guilty. Like I failed that kid, you know? Just feels like everybody can see it on me.
Do you often think that the outcome of the arc-flash accident would have been different if you had acted differently?

I don't know... I mean, I guess I already said I feel like I failed him. But... I don't really sit around trying to figure out what I could've done different. It just happened. I don't want to think about the details of it.
How often do you think about feeling guilty related to the arc-flash accident?
I don't know. A lot, I guess. It's just... always there in the background.
How often do you think about the kid you feel you failed?
I don't really know. I don't keep track of it. I just... I try not to think about him at all, to be honest. So, I'm not sure.
How would you rate the intensity of your guilt feelings on a scale from 1 to 10?
I don't know about a number... an 8 or 9, maybe. I just... I walk around mad and guilty all the time. It feels like I failed that kid and... like everybody can just see it on me. So, yeah. It's high.
